## The Stroop Effect

- Naming the ink color of a word takes longer and is more error prone when the word does not match the color.

## What do we think we know?

::: {.incremental}
- RT continuous
  - Bounded from below: $(0, RT_{max}]$^[The left parenthesis indicates we want to exclude zero; the right bracket indicates we want to include the maximum, but not anything above it.]
  - Or is there an $RT_{min}$?
- $RT_{congruent}<RT_{incongruent}$
- $Accuracy_{congruent}>Accuracy_{incongruent}$
:::

## {.center}

### In Bayesian statistics, these might be called *priors*. {style="text-align: center;"}

## Specify a model (in words)

- RT is equal to the time required to name a word's color
  - Plus more time if the color is...
  
## Specify a model (in words)

- RT is equal to the time required to name a word's color
  - Plus more time if the color is...**incongruent**
  
## Specify a model (in words)

- RT is equal to the time required to name a word's color
  - Plus more time if the color is...**incongruent**
  - Plus random error

## Specify a model (quantitatively)

::: {.incremental}
- Time to name a word's color: $RT_{name-a-color}$
- Extra time if the color is incongruent: $t_{incongruent}$
- Random error: $N(0, sd)$^[Random normal with some standard deviation, *sd*]

:::

::: {.fragment}
$$ RT=RT_{name-a-color}+t_{incongruent}+N(0, sd)$$
:::

## More (simplifying) assumptions

::: {.incremental}
- $RT_{name-a-color}$ is the same for all colors
- $RT_{name-a-color}$ doesn't change across the experiment
- $t_{incongruent}$ doesn't change across the experiment

:::

## More (simplifying) assumptions

::: {.question}
## Is $RT_{name-a-color}$ the same for all people?
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.question}
## Is $t_{incongruent}$ the same for all people?
:::
:::

## Specify the model (as a data picture)

- A ____ plot of RT should show _____

## Specify the model (in code)

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggbeeswarm)
```


```{r}
#| label: make-stroop-data
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
trial <- 1:100
words <- rep(c("Red", "Green", "Blue", "Yellow", "Black"), 20)
word <- sample(x = words, replace = FALSE)
stroop_df <- data.frame(trial, word)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-stroop-trials-by-color
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
#| output-location: slide
stroop_df |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_bar(aes(x = word, fill = word)) +
  scale_color_discrete(c("black", "blue", "green", "red", "yellow"))
```

## How many congruent vs. incongruent trials?

- Let's specify 3/4 trials will be *congruent*
- Make attending to color of text more salient

```{r}
#| label: make-cong-incong-stroop
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
congruency <- rep(c("cong", "cong", "cong", "incong"), 25)
cong_incong <- sample(x = congruency, replace = FALSE)
stroop_df$cong_incong <- cong_incong
```

## Interim check (1 of 2)

```{r}
#| label: view-stroop-data-head
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
head(stroop_df, n = 15)
```

## Interim check (2 of 2)

```{r}
stroop_df |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_bar(aes(x = word, fill = word)) +
  facet_grid(cols = vars(cong_incong))
```

## On to our model

$$ RT=RT_{name-a-color}+t_{incongruent}+N(0, sd)$$

```{r}
#| label: make-stroop-rt-data
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
rt_name_a_color <- 500 # milliseconds
t_incong <- 20
sd_rt <- 10

stroop_df <- stroop_df |>
  mutate(rt = rt_name_a_color + 
           if_else(cong_incong == "incong", t_incong, 0) +
           rnorm(n = 100, sd = sd_rt))
```

## How'd we do?

```{r}
#| label: fig-stroop-histogram
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
#| output-location: slide
stroop_df |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_histogram(aes(x = rt, 
                     fill = cong_incong), bins = 20)
```

## 

```{r}
#| label: fig-stroop-box-violin-effect-size-2.0
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
#| output-location: slide
stroop_df |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_violin(aes(x = rt, y = cong_incong)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(x = rt, y = cong_incong), alpha = .4) +
  geom_beeswarm(aes(x = rt, y = cong_incong), alpha = .5) +
  theme_classic() +
  ylab("Congruency") +
  xlab("RT (ms)") +
  labs(title = "Simulation of a single subject's Stroop data with a 20 ms incongruency effect.")
```

## Effect size

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- The "effect" of some manipulation
- In standard deviation units
- So, $\frac{t_{incong}}{sd_{rt}}$
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
| $t_{incong}$  | $sd_{rt}$ | effect size |
|-----------|-------|-------------|
| 20        | 10    | 2           |
| 10        | 10    | 1           |
| 5         | 10    | 0.5         |
| 2.5       | 10    | 0.25        |
:::
::::

## Modeling right direction/wrong track

- Response variable
- Predictor variable(s)
  - Party registration
  - Vote 2026 likelihood
  - ...

## Specify a model (in words)

- More "Wrong track" among Democrats & Independents
  - Democrats == Independents?
- More "Right direction" among Republicans
- What about Vote 2026 likelihood?

## Specify a model (in code)

```{r}
#| label: right-wrong-make-data
right_wrong_track <- c("wrong", "right", "not_sure")
ds <- sample(right_wrong_track, 100, replace = TRUE, prob = c(.7, .2, .1))
rs <- sample(right_wrong_track, 100, replace = TRUE, prob = c(.3, .5, .2))
ins <- sample(right_wrong_track, 100, replace = TRUE, prob = c(.6, .2, .2))

right_wrong_df <- data.frame(party = rep(c("d", "r", "i"), each = 100),
                             resp = c(ds, rs, ins))
```

---

```{r}
#| label: fig-right-wrong-barplot
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
#| output-location: slide

right_wrong_df |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_bar(aes(x = resp)) +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(party))
```

## Why should we care?

- Simulate your design before you collect data
- What is the data picture you expect?
- Build your data viz pipeline in advance
- Specify your assumptions, check them
- Simulation cheaper than running a study678
